questions.question: Simplify: 2 - [2 - 3{2 - (2 - 4)} div 2]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve innermost bracket first: (2 − 4) = −2.

Then curly braces: {2 − (−2)} = 4.

Then square bracket: [2 − 3 × 4 ÷ 2] = [2 − 6] = −4.

Final value: 2 − (−4) = 6.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: 2 − [2 − 3{2 − (2 − 4)} ÷ 2]

Formula: BODMAS Rule (Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 2 − [2 − 3{2 − (−2)} ÷ 2] ⇒ 2 − [2 − 3{4} ÷ 2] ⇒ 2 − [2 − 12 ÷ 2] ⇒ 2 − [2 − 6] ⇒ 2 − [−4] ⇒ 2 + 4 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the sequence of operations: Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Hierarchy of Brackets

Brackets are solved in the order: small ( ) → curly { } → big/square [ ].

Rule of Signs

The product of two negative signs is always positive (− × − = +).

questions.question: Which of the following ratios is the greatest: 8 : 11, 5 : 7, 13 : 17, or 11 : 13?
questions.solution:

Convert each ratio into its decimal equivalent for quick comparison:

8 : 11 ≈ 0.727

5 : 7 ≈ 0.714

13 : 17 ≈ 0.764

11 : 13 ≈ 0.846

Comparing these values, 0.846 is the greatest.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 : 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given ratios: 8/11, 5/7, 13/17, and 11/13.

To compare fractions, we can either make the denominators equal or convert them to decimals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/83eeaa176ae4f318d982b6c0e295b68b8a401cdcaa363f44c056601685272674.png] ⇒ Decimal value of 8 : 11 = 8 ÷ 11 = 0.7272... ⇒ Decimal value of 5 : 7 = 5 ÷ 7 = 0.7142... ⇒ Decimal value of 13 : 17 = 13 ÷ 17 = 0.7647... ⇒ Decimal value of 11 : 13 = 11 ÷ 13 = 0.8461... ⇒ Comparing the results: 0.8461 > 0.7647 > 0.7272 > 0.7142 ⇒ The largest value is 0.8461, which corresponds to 11 : 13.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 : 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Difference Rule

If the difference between the numerator and denominator is the same for multiple proper fractions, the fraction with the largest numbers is the greatest.

Cross Multiplication Method

To compare a/b and c/d, calculate a × d and b × c. If a × d > b × c, then a/b > c/d.

Proper vs Improper Fractions

A proper fraction (numerator denominator) is always greater than or equal to 1.

questions.question: When a sound is produced, what travels through the medium?

options.text: The disturbance created by the sound source
Both the particles and the disturbance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The disturbance created by the sound source**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sound is a **mechanical wave** that requires a material **medium** (like air, water, or solids) to propagate.
 
• When a sound source vibrates, it creates a **disturbance** in the particles of the medium surrounding it.
 
• The particles of the medium do not travel from the source to the listener's ear. Instead, they **oscillate** or vibrate back and forth about their **mean positions** (equilibrium positions).
 
• The first layer of particles, when disturbed, exerts a force on the next layer, transferring the energy. The original particles then return to their original position, and the **disturbance** moves forward.
 
• Thus, it is the **wave (disturbance)** that moves through the medium, while the individual **particles** of the medium only vibrate locally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sound waves are categorized as **longitudinal waves** because the particles of the medium vibrate in a direction **parallel** to the direction of energy transport.
 
• A longitudinal wave consists of regions of high pressure called **compressions** and regions of low pressure called **rarefactions**.
 
• Sound cannot travel through a **vacuum** because there are no particles to carry the disturbance. This is why sound does not travel in outer space.
 
• The **speed of sound** varies depending on the medium; it generally travels fastest in **solids**, slower in **liquids**, and slowest in **gases** due to the density and elasticity of the material.

questions.question:
From a point in the interior of an equilateral triangle, the length of the perpendiculars to the three sides are 18 cm, 30 cm and 39 cm respectively.

If the area of the triangle is msqrt{k} { cm}² , then find the value of m-k⁷ .
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Height (h) of an equilateral triangle = Sum of perpendiculars from an interior point to the sides.

⇒ h = 18 + 30 + 39 = 87 cm.

Area of equilateral triangle = h² / √3 = 87² / √3 = 7569 / √3 = 2523√3 cm².

Comparing with m√k: m = 2523 and k = 3.

Value of m − k⁷ = 2523 − 3⁷ = 2523 − 2187 = 336.

**∴ The correct answer is 336.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perpendiculars p₁ = 18 cm, p₂ = 30 cm, p₃ = 39 cm.

**Formula Used:**

In an equilateral triangle with side 'a' and height 'h':

h = p₁ + p₂ + p₃

Area = h² / √3

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/592188ff9fde30e1ad219b17204ea7eb117d9f12fbb042b3013e5a843d3746b8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the height of the equilateral triangle be h.

⇒ According to Viviani's Theorem: h = 18 + 30 + 39

⇒ h = 87 cm

⇒ Area = h² / √3

⇒ Area = 87² / √3 = 7569 / √3

⇒ Area = (7569 × √3) / 3 = 2523√3 cm²

⇒ Given Area = m√k

⇒ Comparing both sides: m = 2523 and k = 3

⇒ k⁷ = 3⁷ = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 2187

⇒ Value to find = m − k⁷ = 2523 − 2187

⇒ m − k⁷ = 336

**∴ The correct answer is 336.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Viviani's Theorem

For any interior point in an equilateral triangle, the sum of its distances to the sides is equal to the triangle's altitude: h = p₁ + p₂ + p₃.

Equilateral Triangle Area

The area can be expressed in terms of height (h) as Area = h² / √3 or in terms of side (a) as Area = (√3 / 4) × a².

Relationship between Side and Height

In an equilateral triangle, height h = (√3 / 2) × a, which implies side a = 2h / √3.

Exponent Values of 3

3¹=3, 3²=9, 3³=27, 3⁴=81, 3⁵=243, 3⁶=729, 3⁷=2187.

questions.question: Which of the following is commonly known as the Indian bee?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Apis cerana indica**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Apis cerana indica** is commonly known as the **Indian bee**. It is a sub-species of the Asiatic honey bee and is one of the most common domesticated bee species in **India** and other parts of **Asia**.
 
• **Apis dorsata** is known as the **Rock bee** or **Giant honey bee**. It is a large, wild bee that builds single large combs in open areas like high cliffs or tall buildings. It produces a high amount of honey but is difficult to domesticate due to its aggressive nature.
 
• **Apis florea** is known as the **Little bee**. It is much smaller than other species and builds small nests in bushes and hedges. Its honey yield is very low.
 
• **Apis mellifera** is known as the **European bee** or **Italian bee**. This species is preferred for **commercial honey production** worldwide, including India, because of its high honey-collecting capacity and gentle nature, which makes it easy to domesticate in artificial beehives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The practice of rearing honey bees for the production of honey and wax is called **Apiculture**.
 
• In India, **Apis cerana indica** and **Apis mellifera** are the two primary species used in **beekeeping** for commercial purposes.
 
• Honey is rich in **sugars**, **minerals**, and **enzymes** and is used for its medicinal properties in **Ayurveda**.
 
• Bees also play a crucial role as **pollinators**, helping in the cross-pollination of various agricultural crops, thereby increasing crop yield.

questions.question: Three pipes P, Q and R can fill a tank in 6 hours. After working at it together for 2 hours, R is closed, and P and Q can fill the remaining part in 7 hours. Find the number of hours taken by R alone to fill the tank.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Work done by (P+Q+R) in 2 hours = 2/6 = 1/3 part.

Remaining work = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3 part.

P+Q fill 2/3 part in 7 hours → Full tank in 7 × 3/2 = 10.5 hours.

R efficiency = (1/6) − (1/10.5) = (7 − 4)/42 = 3/42 = 1/14.

R alone will take 14 hours to fill the tank.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Time for (P+Q+R) = 6 hours. Together work = 2 hours. Remaining time for (P+Q) = 7 hours.

Formula: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Pipes
 Time (hr)
 Quantity
 Efficiency
 
 

 P + Q + R
 6
 
 42
 
 7
 
 

 P + Q
 10.5
 4
 
 

Efficiency of R = Efficiency (P+Q+R) − Efficiency (P+Q) = 7 − 4 = 3 units/hr.

⇒ Work done by P, Q and R in 2 hours = 2 ÷ 6 = 1/3 ⇒ Remaining work = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3 ⇒ P and Q fill 2/3 part in 7 hours ⇒ Time for P and Q to fill 1 unit (full tank) = 7 × (3/2) = 10.5 hours ⇒ Total Work (Quantity) = LCM of 6 and 10.5 = 42 units ⇒ Efficiency of R = (42 ÷ 6) − (42 ÷ 10.5) ⇒ Efficiency of R = 7 − 4 = 3 units/hr ⇒ Time taken by R alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of R ⇒ Time = 42 ÷ 3 = 14 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work and Efficiency

Work is the product of time and efficiency. Total work can be assumed as the LCM of individual times to simplify efficiency calculations.

Combined Work Formula

If two pipes fill a tank in 'a' and 'b' hours respectively, then together they fill it in (a × b) ÷ (a + b) hours.

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

Inlet pipes add work (positive efficiency) while outlet or leak pipes subtract work (negative efficiency).

Net profit % = [ 1760 + 435 − 1755 ] / 100

Net profit % = 440 / 100 = 4.4%

**Given:**

**Formula Used:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d9af52d8a80a92abdb39d9b63b0b78f8c77b329f168b114f437118878ff1369.png]

questions.question: A toy is in the form of a solid cone having a radius of 5 cm and a height of 12 cm. It is mounted on a frustum of a solid cone, with the toy’s vertex pointed upwards, and the frustum’s smaller base having a radius of 5 cm. The larger base of the frustum has a radius of 22 cm. Slant height of cone (l) = √(12² + 5²) = 13 cm

LSA of cone = πrl = π × 5 × 13 = 65π

LSA of frustum = π(R + r)L = π(22 + 5) × 32 = 864π

Area of bottom base = πR² = π × 22² = 484π

Total Surface Area = (65 + 864 + 484)π = 1413π

**∴ The correct answer is 1413π.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of cone (r) = 5 cm, Height of cone (h) = 12 cm

Smaller radius of frustum (r) = 5 cm, Larger radius of frustum (R) = 22 cm

Slant height of frustum (L) = 32 cm

**Formula used:**

Slant height of cone (l) = √(h² + r²)

TSA of toy = LSA of cone + LSA of frustum + Area of larger base

TSA = πrl + π(R + r)L + πR²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02df95399269bb1c3f80afaaebd34b98a1494ad34fffb44093385b6bf2267bf9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Slant height of cone (l) = √(12² + 5²) = √(144 + 25) = √169 = 13 cm

⇒ Curved surface area of cone = π × 5 × 13 = 65π cm²

⇒ Curved surface area of frustum = π × (22 + 5) × 32 = π × 27 × 32

⇒ 27 × 32 = 864π cm²

⇒ Area of the larger circular base = π × 22² = 484π cm²

⇒ Total surface area of the toy = 65π + 864π + 484π

⇒ Total surface area = (65 + 864 + 484)π = 1413π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1413π.**

Surface Area of Cone

Lateral Surface Area = πrl and Total Surface Area = πr(l + r), where l is slant height.

Surface Area of Frustum

Lateral Surface Area = πL(R + r) and Total Surface Area = πL(R + r) + πR² + πr².

Volume of Frustum

Volume = (1/3)πH(R² + r² + R×r), where H is the vertical height of the frustum.

Slant Height of Frustum

L = √[H² + (R − r)²], where H is vertical height and R, r are radii.

questions.question: On reaching an organ or tissue, arteries divide into smaller and smaller vessels. The smallest vessels have walls that are one cell thick and are called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**capillaries**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Capillaries** are the smallest and most numerous of the blood vessels, forming a connection between the vessels that carry blood away from the heart (**arteries**) and the vessels that return blood to the heart (**veins**).
 
• The primary function of capillaries is the **exchange of materials** (oxygen, nutrients, and waste products) between the blood and tissue cells.
 
• The walls of capillaries are composed of a single layer of **endothelial cells**, making them only **one cell thick**. This extremely thin structure allows substances to pass through easily via **diffusion**.
 
• While **arterioles** are smaller branches of arteries that lead to capillaries, they still possess muscular walls and are thicker than a single cell layer.
 
• **Arteries** and **veins** have much thicker walls consisting of three distinct layers: the tunica intima, tunica media, and tunica externa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The diameter of a capillary is so small (about 5 to 10 micrometers) that **red blood cells** often have to pass through them in **single file**.
 
• The total network of capillaries in the human body is called a **capillary bed**, which provides a massive surface area for gas exchange.
 
• In the lungs, **pulmonary capillaries** surround the **alveoli** to facilitate the uptake of oxygen and the release of carbon dioxide.
 
• Unlike arteries, **veins** contain **valves** to prevent the backflow of blood as it moves against gravity toward the heart.

questions.question: A machine does 1000 J of work in 5 seconds. Its power is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Power** is defined as the **rate of doing work** or the rate at which energy is transferred or transformed.
 
• The standard formula to calculate **Power (P)** is the amount of **Work Done (W)** divided by the **Time Taken (t)**: Power = Work / Time.
 
• According to the question, the machine performs **1000 Joules (J)** of work in a duration of **5 seconds (s)**.
 
• By substituting these values into the formula: Power = 1000 J / 5 s = **200 Watts (W)**.
 
• This indicates that the machine is capable of converting or using 200 Joules of energy every single second.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **SI unit** of power is the **Watt (W)**, named in honor of the Scottish engineer **James Watt**.
 
• One Watt is defined as the power of an agent which does work at the rate of **one Joule per second** (1 W = 1 J/s).
 
• **Power** is a **scalar quantity** because it only possesses magnitude and does not have a direction.
 
• Other units of power include the **Kilowatt (kW)**, where 1 kW = 1000 W, and **Horsepower (hp)**, which is commonly used in the automotive industry (1 hp is approximately equal to **746 Watts**).
 
• If the work is done at a non-uniform rate, we calculate **Average Power** by dividing the total work done by the total time taken.

questions.question: If mean of 10 observations x₁, x₂, dots x₁₀ is 20, then the value of sumᵢ₌₁¹⁰ ( (3x_i-4)/(5) ) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If every observation x is transformed to (ax − b)/c, the new mean becomes (a × Old Mean − b)/c.

New Mean = (3 × 20 − 4) ÷ 5 = 56 ÷ 5 = 11.2

Sum of 10 observations = New Mean × Total Observations = 11.2 × 10 = 112

**∴ The correct answer is 112.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of observations (n) = 10

Mean of observations (−x) = 20

**Formula Used:**

Mean (−x) = (∑xᵢ) ÷ n

∑(axᵢ − b) = a∑xᵢ − (n × b)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/83940e157d78379f61d2d8f440f4777982e09e30e58a7e8bee04d1f5ec9c688f.png] 

⇒ Total sum of 10 observations (∑xᵢ) = n × Mean = 10 × 20 = 200

⇒ Required value = ∑ᵢ₌₁¹⁰ ((3xᵢ − 4) ÷ 5)

⇒ Required value = (1 ÷ 5) × ∑ᵢ₌₁¹⁰ (3xᵢ − 4)

⇒ Required value = (1 ÷ 5) × [3 × ∑xᵢ − ∑4]

⇒ Required value = (1 ÷ 5) × [3 × 200 − (10 × 4)]

⇒ Required value = (1 ÷ 5) × [600 − 40]

⇒ Required value = 560 ÷ 5 = 112

**∴ The correct answer is 112.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Transformation of Mean

If yᵢ = axᵢ + b, then the new mean −y = a−x + b. This shows mean is affected by both change of origin and scale.

The sum of the deviations of a set of observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero: ∑(xᵢ − −x) = 0.

Arithmetic Mean Property

If a constant k is subtracted from each observation, the mean of the new observations is (−x − k).

questions.question: If 4x² + (1)/(4x²) = 14 , what is the positive value of x + (1)/(4x) ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Value of (2x + 1/2x)² = (4x² + 1/4x²) + 2

Substituting given: (2x + 1/2x)² = 14 + 2 = 16

Square root gives 2x + 1/2x = 4

Divide by 2 to get x + 1/4x = 4 ÷ 2 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: 4x² + 1/4x² = 14

Formula: (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

⇒ (2x)² + (1/2x)² = 14

⇒ (2x + 1/2x)² − 2 × (2x) × (1/2x) = 14

⇒ (2x + 1/2x)² − 2 = 14

⇒ (2x + 1/2x)² = 16

⇒ 2x + 1/2x = √16

⇒ 2x + 1/2x = 4

⇒ 2(x + 1/4x) = 4

⇒ x + 1/4x = 4 ÷ 2

⇒ x + 1/4x = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Binomial Square Identity

The fundamental identity (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab is used to find sums of squares from the sum of terms.

Reciprocal Relations

For any term x + 1/x = k, the value of x² + 1/x² is always k² − 2.

Difference of Squares

The identity (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab can be used if the question involves a negative sign between terms.

questions.question: Which of the following functions of mitochondria makes it a powerhouse of the cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Generation of ATP**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria** are known as the **powerhouse of the cell** because they are the primary site for **cellular respiration**, which produces energy.
 
• The main function of mitochondria is the **generation of ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate), which serves as the **energy currency** for various biological processes in the cell.
 
• During the **Krebs cycle** and **oxidative phosphorylation** occurring within the mitochondria, chemical energy from nutrients is converted into ATP.
 
• While mitochondria can produce some **heat** (especially in brown adipose tissue) and contain various **enzymes** for metabolic pathways, it is specifically the production of **ATP** that earns them the title of 'powerhouse'.
 
• **NADPH** is primarily generated in the **Pentose Phosphate Pathway** in the cytoplasm or during the light reactions of **photosynthesis** in chloroplasts, not as the primary 'power' output of mitochondria.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria** are **double-membrane** bound organelles found in most **eukaryotic** organisms.
 
• The inner membrane of the mitochondria is folded into numerous finger-like projections called **cristae**, which increase the surface area for **ATP synthesis**.
 
• Mitochondria are **semi-autonomous** organelles because they possess their own **DNA (mtDNA)** and **ribosomes** (70S), allowing them to produce some of their own proteins.
 
• Apart from energy production, they play vital roles in **calcium storage**, **apoptosis** (programmed cell death), and the regulation of **cellular metabolism**.
 
• They are absent in **prokaryotic cells** and mature **mammalian red blood cells**.

questions.question: The reaction of sodium hydrogen carbonate upon heating produces:

options.text: Sodium hydroxide, oxygen, and carbon monoxide at high temperature
Sodium carbonate, water, and carbon dioxide gas during cooking
Sodium chloride, water, and hydrogen gas under normal heating
Sodium sulfate, hydrogen, and carbon dioxide when strongly heated

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium carbonate, water, and carbon dioxide gas during cooking**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **Sodium hydrogen carbonate** (also known as **Baking soda**) is heated during the process of cooking, it undergoes **thermal decomposition**.
 
• The reaction involves the breakdown of the compound into **Sodium carbonate**, **Water**, and **Carbon dioxide** gas.
 
• The balanced chemical equation for this reaction is: 2NaHCO₃ xrightarrow{Heat} Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ 
 
• The **Carbon dioxide** gas produced during this reaction is responsible for making cakes and bread **rise**, giving them a soft and spongy texture.
 
• **Sodium hydroxide** and **oxygen** are not produced in this reaction, making option 1 incorrect. **Sodium chloride** and **Sodium sulfate** are not produced because there are no chlorine or sulfur atoms in the reactant **Sodium hydrogen carbonate**, making options 3 and 4 incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baking Soda** is chemically represented as NaHCO₃ and is a mild **non-corrosive basic salt**.
 
• It is produced using the **Solvay process**, where **sodium chloride**, **ammonia**, and **carbon dioxide** react in water.
 
• Aside from cooking, it is used as an **antacid** to neutralize excess acid in the stomach (providing relief from **acidity**).
 
• It is also a primary component in **soda-acid fire extinguishers** because the release of CO₂ helps to smother the fire.
 
• **Baking powder** is a mixture of baking soda and a mild edible acid like **tartaric acid**. When baking powder is heated or mixed in water, the acid reacts with the soda to release CO₂ gas.

questions.question: Why is a colloid considered stable?

options.text: Its particles react chemically with the dispersion medium.
Its particles can be separated easily by filtration.
Its particles do not settle down when left undisturbed.
Its particles dissolve completely in the dispersion medium.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Its particles do not settle down when left undisturbed.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **colloid** is considered **stable** because its particles remain suspended in the **dispersion medium** indefinitely and do not aggregate or settle at the bottom of the container under the influence of gravity when left **undisturbed**.
 
• The stability of a colloid is primarily due to **Brownian motion**, which is the continuous, random zigzag motion of colloidal particles caused by collisions with molecules of the dispersion medium. This motion opposes the force of gravity.
 
• Another factor contributing to stability is the presence of **similar electrical charges** on all the particles of a given colloid. These like charges **repel** each other, preventing the particles from coming together to form larger, heavier aggregates that would otherwise settle out.
 
• In contrast, a **suspension** is unstable because its larger particles eventually settle down, while a **true solution** is stable because the solute particles are completely dissolved at the molecular or ionic level.
 
• Colloidal particles are too small to be seen with the naked eye and cannot be separated by **ordinary filtration** because they pass through the pores of filter paper.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tyndall Effect**: Colloids are known for scattering a beam of light, making the path of light visible. This phenomenon is a hallmark characteristic of colloidal systems.
 
• The size of **colloidal particles** typically ranges between **1 nanometer and 1000 nanometers** (10⁻⁹ to 10⁻⁶ meters).
 
• Common examples of colloids include **milk**, **fog**, **smoke**, **blood**, and **gelatin**.
 
• Colloids consist of two phases: the **dispersed phase** (the substance distributed) and the **dispersion medium** (the medium in which it is distributed).
 
• While they cannot be filtered normally, colloidal particles can be separated using a specialized technique called **centrifugation** or **ultrafiltration**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines refraction of light?

options.text: Bending of light when it falls on a mirror
Change in direction of light when it passes from one medium to another
Scattering of light by air molecules
Splitting of light into seven colours

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Change in direction of light when it passes from one medium to another**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Refraction** is defined as the phenomenon where **light rays** change their direction or bend when they travel from one **transparent medium** to another with a different **optical density**.
 
• This change in direction happens because the **speed of light** varies in different media. For instance, light travels slower in **glass** or **water** than it does in **air** or a **vacuum**.
 
• **Reflection** (Option 1) occurs when light bounces off a polished surface like a **mirror**, rather than passing through it.
 
• **Scattering** (Option 3) is the process where light is deflected in various directions by **air molecules**, dust, or water droplets.
 
• **Dispersion** (Option 4) is the **splitting of white light** into its seven constituent colours (VIBGYOR) when it passes through a **prism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The extent of bending is determined by the **Refractive Index** (n) of the material, which is the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in that medium.
 
• According to **Snell’s Law**, the relationship between the angles of incidence and refraction is given by: n₁ sin theta₁ = n₂ sin theta₂ .
 
• When light travels from an **optically rarer medium** (lower refractive index) to an **optically denser medium** (higher refractive index), it bends **towards the normal**.
 
• Conversely, when light travels from a **denser medium** to a **rarer medium**, it bends **away from the normal**.
 
• Natural phenomena caused by refraction include the **twinkling of stars**, the **early sunrise and delayed sunset**, and the **apparent displacement** of objects submerged in water.

questions.question: A 12 m tall building casts a shadow of 8 m at a certain time of the day. At the same time, a vertical pole with a flag on top casts a shadow of 15 m. If the height of the flag alone is 3 m, find the height of the pole.

Total Height (Pole + Flag) = 15 × (3 ÷ 2) = 22.5 m

Pole Height = Total Height − Flag Height = 22.5 − 3 = 19.5 m

**∴ The correct answer is 19.5 m.**

Height of building = 12 m

Shadow of building = 8 m

Height₁ / Shadow₁ = Height₂ / Shadow₂ (Since the angle of elevation of the sun is the same)

⇒ Let the total height of the pole and flag be H.

⇒ 12 / 8 = H / 15

⇒ 1.5 = H / 15

⇒ H = 1.5 × 15

⇒ H = 22.5 m

⇒ Height of Pole = Total Height − Height of Flag

⇒ Height of Pole = 22.5 − 3

⇒ Height of Pole = 19.5 m

**∴ The correct answer is 19.5 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Similar Triangles

If A:B = C:D, then the product of extremes equals the product of means (A × D = B × C). Here, 12 × 15 = 8 × H.

• The power to amend the **Constitution of India** is vested in the **Parliament** under **Article 368** of **Part XX**. This article ensures that the Constitution can be adapted to changing circumstances without losing its identity.
 
• A **Constitutional Amendment** can only be initiated by introducing a bill for the purpose in either **House of Parliament** (the **Lok Sabha** or the **Rajya Sabha**), and not in the state legislatures. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*
 
• An **Executive Order** is a directive issued by the **President** or the **Government** to manage the operations of the executive branch; it does not have the authority to alter constitutional provisions. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• While the **Supreme Court** has the power of **Judicial Review** to interpret the Constitution and strike down laws that violate its **Basic Structure**, it cannot proactively "change" or "add" provisions to the Constitution. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• A **Presidential Ordinance** is issued under **Article 123** when **Parliament** is not in session. While an ordinance has the same force and effect as an **Act of Parliament**, it cannot be used to amend the **Constitution of India**. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
• For a **Constitutional Amendment Bill**, there is no provision for a **joint sitting** of both the Houses in case of a disagreement, unlike ordinary bills.

• **Types of Amendments:**

 
 
• **By Simple Majority:** Certain provisions like the formation of **new states**, changes in **names and boundaries** of states, and salaries of judges can be amended by a **simple majority** (more than **50%** of members present and voting). These are not considered amendments under **Article 368**.
 
• **By Special Majority:** Most provisions, including **Fundamental Rights** and **Directive Principles of State Policy**, require a **special majority** (a majority of the total membership of each House and a majority of **two-thirds** of the members present and voting).
 
• **By Special Majority and Ratification:** Provisions affecting the **federal structure** (like **Election of the President** or powers of the **Supreme Court**) require a special majority plus ratification by the legislatures of at least **half of the states** by a simple majority.
 
 
 
• **The President's Role:** After being passed by both Houses, the bill is presented to the **President**, who **must give assent**. The President can neither withhold assent nor return the bill for reconsideration, as per the **24th Amendment Act of 1971**.
 
• **Basic Structure Doctrine:** In the landmark **Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)**, the **Supreme Court** ruled that **Parliament** cannot use its amending power to alter the **"Basic Structure"** of the Constitution, such as **Secularism**, **Democracy**, and **Federalism**.

• **Significant Amendments:**

 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act (1976):** Often called the **'Mini-Constitution'**, it added the words **'Socialist'**, **'Secular'**, and **'Integrity'** to the **Preamble** and introduced **Fundamental Duties**.
 
• **44th Amendment Act (1978):** Enacted by the **Janata Government** to nullify many of the distortions introduced during the **Emergency**.
 
• **101st Amendment Act (2016):** Introduced the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** across the country, requiring ratification by more than half of the states.
 
• **106th Amendment Act (2023):** Known as the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**, it provides **33% reservation** for women in the **Lok Sabha** and **State Legislative Assemblies**.
